title: France's AFD lines up €100 million climate loan and €40 million for water and sanitation
excerpt: The commitments came out of the annual Bangladesh and AFD consultation in Paris. AFD also plans to move into technical and vocational training from 2029.
content:
France's development agency, Agence Française de Développement (AFD), has agreed in principle to a €100 million climate policy loan for Bangladesh in 2027 and €40 million for water supply and sanitation in 2028, according to an Economic Relations Division (ERD) press release reported by Bangladesh Post on 12 November.

The pipeline was agreed at the seventh annual consultation meeting between the government and AFD at AFD's headquarters in Paris. ERD Secretary Md Shahriar Kader Siddiky and Cyrille Bellier, AFD's head of department for Europe, the Middle East and Asia, co-chaired the meeting. AFD Country Director Cynthia Mela also attended.

Key points

  • Pipeline: a €100 million climate policy loan in 2027 and €40 million for water and sanitation in 2028. Loan terms were not published.
  • Current portfolio: 12 ongoing projects worth $1.75 billion, almost all of it loans. Grants make up only $18.6 million.
  • New areas: from 2029-2030, AFD plans to expand into technical and vocational education and training (TVET), skills and lending to non-government borrowers.
  • Capacity fund: both sides signed an amended agreement for AFD's Expertise and Capacity Building Fund (FERC).

Why it matters

AFD is one of Bangladesh's larger bilateral lenders, and its money comes almost entirely as loans. A policy loan goes to the national budget against agreed reforms, not to specific projects, so the climate policy conditions attached to it will be worth reading when they are published. The planned move into non-sovereign financing could open AFD credit lines to banks, microfinance institutions and large NGOs. That fits the trend Devlens described in its report on NGOs shifting from services to lending.

What to watch

The reform conditions in the climate policy loan, and which agencies and towns are chosen for the water and sanitation money.

Sources

  • Bangladesh secures €100m climate loan, €40m for water, sanitation, Bangladesh Post (ERD press release via BSS), 12 November 2026
